tools.name: tool/activation_hint
tools.description: Returns the active discovery mode (full/search), the env var knob, and compact counts for the canonical discovery surfaces. Use this to detect that tools/list is intentionally thinned and that the agent should reach for tool/get_relevant_tools. Pass verbose=true to include the full tool-key array for the search manifest. Safe. Example: {} → {"mode":"search","searchSurfaceCount":6} Keywords: activation, discovery mode, full, search, env var

verbose.description: When true, includes the full searchSurface array. Default false for token-frugal summaries.

envVar.description: Env-var name the operator can tweak.

searchSurfaceCount.description: Size of the search-only manifest the kernel would advertise.

searchSurface.description: Tool keys in the search-only manifest (sorted ordinal). Present only when verbose=true.

tools.description: Returns the kernel catalog grouped by capability bucket (rendering, audio, ai, physics, …). Use this to browse a whole capability when the query is exploratory rather than verb-specific. Safe. Example: {"capability":"spawning"} → {"capability":"spawning","tools":[{"name":"actor/spawn","group":"actor"}],"count":2} Keywords: capability, bucket, browse, group, filter, domain

capability.description: Optional bucket filter (e.g. 'audio'). When omitted, every bucket is returned.

includeHidden.description: When true, hibernated atomics are included. Default false.

verbose.description: When true, includes the full `tools[]` array per bucket. Default false for count-only summaries.

buckets.description: Each bucket: {name, count} by default; `tools[]` is included only when verbose=true.

tools.name: tool/get_relevant_tools
tools.description: R8-03 lazy-discovery meta-tool. Given a natural-language intent (e.g. 'fade audio when player dies', 'spawn a rigid body', 'rotate the camera'), returns the top-K tools most likely to satisfy it, ranked by the Wave 2 semantic-router substrate. Supports optional policy filter (safe/mutating/destructive) to scope results by tool safety level — use policy='safe' for read-only exploration to reduce wrong-tool selection risk. Profile-aware: by default respects the session's active profile/switch filter; pass profile='core' (or any registered profile name) to override for one call. Return envelope is trimmed for context-budget friendliness: [{ tool, score, summary, bucket, policy }]. Pair with tool/inspect for the full schema of a candidate. Calls this instead of tools/list when you need 1-of-N tool resolution rather than the full catalog. Safe. Keywords: get relevant tools, discovery, rank, intent, semantic, profile, policy, lazy. Example: {"intent":"spawn a cube","k":5,"policy":"safe"} → {"count":3,"profileApplied":"session","matches":[{"tool":"actor/spawn","score":0.9,"summary":"Spawns a new actor","bucket":"actor","policy":"safe"}]}

intent.description: Natural-language description of the task the AI needs a tool for. Verb-noun phrasing works best ("spawn actor", "play audio", "set fog density").

k.description: Top-K cap. Default 8; hard cap 50. Higher K trades wire size for completeness; the ranker already filters zero-score candidates so K is an upper bound, not a quota.

profile.description: Optional profile override (e.g. 'core', 'lite', 'physics', 'all'). When set, only tools whose group is in the named profile are considered; the session's active filter is ignored for this call. When omitted, the session's active filter applies (set via profile/switch / tool/set_enabled).

capability.description: Optional capability bucket filter (e.g. 'audio', 'rendering'). Applied AFTER ranking so the ranker can still use the bucket signal during scoring.

groups.description: Optional STATELESS per-call group filter (e.g. ["scene", "actor", "material"]). Only tools whose extracted group (from the tool key prefix) is in this list are returned. ANDs with any profile or capability filter. Completely independent of session state. Absent or empty = no group filtering applied. ALIAS: 'groups' is the backwards-compatible name for the canonical 'tags' parameter. Use 'tags' in new code.

tags.description: Optional STATELESS per-call tag filter (e.g. ["scene", "actor", "material"]). Tags are the canonical name for tool group prefixes — every tool's group (from the key prefix before '/') is a tag. Only tools whose tag is in this list are returned. ANDs with any profile or capability filter. Completely independent of session state. Absent or empty = no tag filtering. When both 'tags' and 'groups' are provided, the intersection is applied.

includeSchemas.description: When true, each result includes the tool's full inputSchema. Default false for token-budget friendliness — pair with tool/inspect when you need the schema of a specific candidate.

verbose.description: When true, includes diagnostic fields in the response: intent echo, k echo, capability echo, elapsedMs. Default false for token-budget friendliness.

policy.description: Filter results by safety policy. 'safe' = only Policy.Safe tools. 'mutating' = Safe + Mutating. 'destructive' = all. Default: 'destructive' (all). Use 'safe' for read-only/exploration tasks to reduce wrong-tool selection risk.

profileApplied.description: Name of the profile filter applied; 'session' when the session filter was used, 'none' when no filter applied, or the literal profile name when explicitly overridden.

matches.description: Trimmed envelope per hit: { tool, score, summary, bucket, policy }. Top-3 hits also include an argHints string (compact "name:type, name?:type, …"). When includeSchemas=true, also includes inputSchema per hit.

lowConfidence.description: True when every returned score is below 1.0, meaning no query token achieved even a single exact key-segment match. Consider broadening the query. Absent = false.

receiptId.description: Auto-injected for Mutating/Destructive tools. Look up via mutation/get_receipt.

receiptUtc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the receipt (auto-injected).

tools.name: tool/health
tools.description: Returns kernel health: bridge availability, live compile readiness, tool count, server posture, and any warnings that AI clients should react to (e.g. Live bridge not attached or the latest editor compile failed). Example: {} → {"status":"healthy","kernelVersion":"1.0.0","uptime":"01:23:45"} Keywords: health, kernel, bridge, compile, status, workMode, toolCount, diagnostics

verbose.description: When true, includes extended transport and discovery bookkeeping fields such as minimal_mode_tokens, contract_count, and profile_active. Default false for compact health checks.

healthy.description: True when the bridge is live and the editor compile lane is ready for real work (not compiling, not failed). False means AI clients must stop before claiming the repo is healthy.

workMode.description: One dumb-proof workflow state: 'editor_off_codework' | 'live_compiling' | 'live_compile_broken' | 'live_not_ready' | 'live_ready'. AI clients should branch on this field first.

readOnly.description: True when FLAXMCP_READONLY env var is set; AI clients should skip Mutating/Destructive calls.

can.description: Tiny capability map for the current mode: { editCode, runScopedBuilds, runTests, verifyGameSide, useEditorTools, hotReload }.

nextAction.description: Short operator/AI hint for the current workMode.

compile.description: Live compile-lane summary: { status:'ok'|'compiling'|'compile_failed'|'not_ready'|'no_editor', isCompiling, isReady, lastFailed, compilationsCount, errorCount?, warningCount?, buildFailed?, logPath?, sampleErrorCodes? }.

warnings.description: Marathon cleanup 2026-05-21 (P0b): array of structured-warning rows when the kernel state is non-ideal (e.g. {code:'bridge_unavailable', message:'Live bridge not attached - editor verbs will return mode:standalone. Driver scripts should FAIL FAST.'}). Absent or empty array when everything is healthy.

routing.description: Routing-model diagnostics (2026-07-31): { queryRouter: {enabled, reason, modelVariant}, intentClassifier: {enabled, reason, modelVariant}, abstainConfidenceThreshold, abstainMarginThreshold }. reason is a stable category token (e.g. not_configured, model_load_failed, enabled) and modelVariant identifies the active backend (e.g. onnx-query-router-4class, fallback-route-llm, none). No filesystem paths, env-var names, credentials, or arbitrary detail are ever exposed.

tools.name: tool/inspect
tools.description: Returns the full descriptor envelope for one tool: key, group, action, policy, schemas, mega action map, UX hints, capability bucket. The follow-up to a top-1 tool/get_relevant_tools hit when the AI wants the schema before calling. Set schemaShape='flat' for a no-$ref JSON-Schema argSchema (planner-pasteable; replaces the former tool/get_advanced_tool). Set actionsOnly=true for just a mega's sub-action enum (cheap navigation; replaces the former tool/list_actions). Also returns hiddenFromDefaultView (true when a manage_X mega covers this tool, so it stays registered but drops from the default tools/list view). Returns found=false (not an error) on an unknown key so callers can branch without try/catch. Safe. Example: {"name":"scene/info"} → {"name":"scene/info","group":"scene","policy":"Safe","title":"Get Scene Info","description":"Returns loaded scene count...","args":[{"name":"none"}],"returns":[{"name":"loadedSceneCount","type":"integer"}]} Keywords: inspect, tool, schema, details, descriptor, mega actions, UX

schemaShape.description: Argument-schema rendering. 'nested' (default) returns the full SchemaBuilder input/output schemas (with $ref/$defs expansion). 'flat' returns a single-level argSchema {type:object, properties, required} with no $ref — directly pasteable into a planner prompt (former tool/get_advanced_tool shape).

actionsOnly.description: When true, returns ONLY { key, found, isMega, actions:[{name, atomic, policy}] } for a mega-tool — the cheapest navigation envelope (former tool/list_actions shape). Ignored for non-mega tools (they have no sub-actions). Default false.

found.description: False when the key is not in the kernel catalog (the rest of the envelope is omitted). True otherwise.

hiddenFromDefaultView.description: True when the tool is registered but hidden from the default tools/list view (a manage_X mega covers its group, or the group is hibernated). Found=true + hidden=true means the tool EXISTS but is mega-covered — reach it through the mega's actions.

tools.name: tool/recent
tools.description: Returns the tools called in the recent session window, oldest-first. Sources from the kernel's receipt FTS5 backend (existing observability store; no new persistence layer). Lets AIs resume the previous session flow without re-discovering. Safe. Example: {"limit":5} → {"tools":[{"name":"scene/info","calledAt":"2026-05-01T12:00:00Z"}],"count":1} Keywords: recent, tools, history, session, resume, receipts

window.description: Recency window as a duration string: '15m', '1h', '24h'. Default '1h'. Parsed as fall-back to 1 hour on garbled input.

limit.description: Cap on receipts walked. Default 50; hard cap 500.

tools.description: Each entry: {key, calls, lastUtc, lastOutcome, bucket}.
